issues: Broken Markdown structure: original has heading '#### Pasal 18 ayat (6) ...' but translation renders it as '#### Article 18 paragraph (6) ...' (should remain a 'Pasal/Article' heading, not 'Article 18' of the Constitution). This is a meaning drift and mislabels the heading.

Meaning drift: 'Pasal 18 ayat (6) Undang-Undang Dasar ...' refers to Article 18(6) of the Constitution, not 'Article 18 paragraph (6)' as a standalone section heading; the heading should reflect 'Article 18 paragraph (6) of the 1945 Constitution...' without implying it is a policy article heading.

Broken Markdown structure: original has heading '#### Pasal 18 ayat (6) ...' but translation renders it as '#### Article 18 paragraph (6) ...' (should remain a 'Pasal/Article' heading, not a constitutional article).

Meaning drift: 'Pasal 18 ayat (6) Undang-Undang Dasar...' refers to Article 18(6) of the Constitution, not a section heading 'Article 18 paragraph (6)'—the heading should be '#### Article 18 paragraph (6) of the 1945 Constitution...' only if the original heading is 'Pasal 18 ayat (6)...' as a citation; however the original uses 'Pasal' as part of the citation, so translation should not imply it is a document section heading of this regulation. It should be translated as a citation line without changing its role.
Scrambled/merged list markers in Article 2: items c and d are merged; item i is merged into h ("andi.")
Scrambled/merged list markers in Article 3: item f is prefixed with stray "6" and item j is merged into i ("andj.")
Scrambled/merged list markers in Article 4: item g is merged into f ("andg.")
Minor meaning drift/grammar in Article 13 definition: "taken to victims" should be "taken for the victim" (service/action to be taken for the victim)
Missing terminal punctuation in Article 1 item 12 (should end with a period, consistent with list items)

Scrambled/altered list structure in Article 2: original has merged markers/text ("c. ...d.", "h. ...dani."); translation normalizes into separate items and omits the stray "dan" placement, changing the marker/text sequence required downstream.

Scrambled/altered list structure in Article 3: original has merged marker/text ("e. ... 6f.") and merged conjunction/marker ("danj."); translation splits into separate f. and adds a standalone "and" line, changing marker/text sequence.
Scrambled/altered list structure in Article 4: original has merged conjunction/marker ("dang."); translation splits into separate g. and adds a standalone "and" line, changing marker/text sequence.

Meaning drift: Article 2 item c in the original includes the text "pemenuhan hak anakd." (i.e., includes the trailing "d." as part of the same line); translation removed that artifact, so the translated text no longer preserves the original content/structure exactly.

Scrambled/merged list markers in multiple places: '8h.', 'andl.', 'andf.', 'andc.', 'ande.' are stuck to preceding text; Article 12 also merges '1.' with 'a.' and 'd.' with 'e.'; these must be separated so each list item marker appears once and in order.
Broken list structure in Article 8 and Article 12 where 'for:' is immediately followed by 'a.' without a line break, obscuring the sub-list boundary (downstream splitting risk).

Scrambled list/numbering markers in the original (e.g., "g. ...; 8h." and "danl.", "andf.") were normalized in the translation; downstream requires preserving the original markers exactly and in order.

Article 12 paragraph numbering: in the original, items (2) and (3) are inline markers within the same article block; translation changed formatting by placing (2) and (3) on new lines without preserving the original inline structure.

Minor meaning drift: "Paragraf 2" under Article 10 is titled "Pencegahan" (Prevention) but Article 10 text is about prevention; translation says "in order to prevent" (ok) but the original heading structure must be preserved exactly; also ensure "preventing violence" vs "preventing violations" matches each article (Article 10 is about preventing violence; Article 11 about preventing violations of rights).

Scrambled/merged list markers: several lettered items are concatenated (e.g., 'include:a.', 'andd.', 'andc.', '14f.', 'andg.', 'form of:a.', 'andf.', 'andh.', 'conditions:a.', 'and/ord.') which breaks list structure required for downstream splitting.

Numbering marker formatting inconsistency: Article 30 paragraph (2) is on a new line as '(2)' while others use '2.'; keep markers present and ordered but normalize to match original structure (1., 2., 3.).
Scrambled/corrupted list markers in Article 21: original has items f and g, but translation shows "14f." and "ang." instead of "f." and "g."
Scrambled/corrupted list marker in Article 28(2): original has item e, but translation shows "16e." instead of "e."

Scrambled/merged list structure: in multiple places the list markers (a., b., etc.) are merged into the preceding text (e.g., 'responsible for:a.', 'andh.', 'andd.', 'andl.', 'and/ore.', 'and/orc.', 'andb.', 'andc.'), breaking item boundaries compared to the original.

Minor meaning drift/terminology: 'Perangkat Daerah' should be 'Regional Apparatus' (not 'Regional Apparatus' is fine) but 'Perangat Daerah' typo in original; keep meaning—no change needed beyond structure. Main correction is structural to preserve markers and order.

Heading mismatch: original has "## Bagian ketiga" (lowercase 'ketiga') before Parents and Family, but translation uses "## Part Three"; headings must match exactly in level and position, including this distinct heading text.

Meaning drift in Article 35(1): "panti sosial" translated as "social institutions"; should be "social homes/shelters" (social care institutions) to reflect a facility (panti), not generic institutions.

Scrambled/merged list markers and numbering: several sub-items are concatenated (e.g., 'andd.', 'andc.', 'and/ord.', 'andb.', 'ande.') and some paragraph markers are inconsistent ((2) appears while others use 1., 3., 4., 5.). This can break downstream boundary splitting.
Minor meaning drift/terminology: 'Pemulangan' is translated as 'Repatriation' (can imply cross-border); more accurate is 'Return' (to area of origin).
Scrambled/merged list structure in Article 58(3): lettered items a–l are run together (e.g., 'means:a.'), and stray '29' appears before item b; item l is merged into 'and/orl.'
Scrambled/merged list structure in Article 59: items a and b are merged into 'andb.'
Minor meaning/format drift: 'Article1' should be 'Article 1' to match the original 'Pasal1' spacing/structure; keep as a single line but correct spacing

Scrambled list/numbering structure in Article 58(3): original has inline markers and a stray page number "29" causing merged items ("cara:a." and "Daerah; 29b." and "dan/ataul."); translation normalizes into a clean a–l list, which changes the marker structure required downstream.
Scrambled list/numbering structure in Article 59: original has merged markers ("a. ...;danb."); translation splits into separate lines, altering marker placement/structure required downstream.
